name: ES Closing Auction-Density Switch v1
instrument: ES transaction-price and volume signal executed with one MES using recorded MBP-1 quotes
source: Databento GLBX.MDP3 ES trades and MES MBP-1
hypothesis: Equal-duration closing-auction halves reveal whether a late price move was densely negotiated or crossed a liquidity vacuum. Rising volume per visited price level indicates acceptance and should preserve the second-half move; falling density indicates fragile displacement that should reverse.

signal.half_density: sum of transaction size divided by count of distinct transaction prices in that half
signal.second_half_displacement: last transaction price minus first transaction price in the second half
signal.dense_transition: second-half density is greater than or equal to first-half density; follow second-half displacement
signal.vacuum_transition: second-half density is less than first-half density; fade second-half displacement
signal.zero_or_missing_rule: no trade if second-half displacement is zero, either half has no trades, or a required value is missing

execution.entry_time: first MES MBP-1 record at or after 15:30:05 ET
execution.stop: none; one MES and a fixed approximately 29-minute holding period bound exposure
execution.exit_time: first recorded MES MBP-1 quote at or after 15:59:45 ET
execution.position_limit: one MES and at most one trade per RTH session

economics.slippage_model: the full recorded MES bid-ask spread is crossed at entry and exit; no additional modeled slippage

lesson: Volume per visited price level was not a stable acceptance measure. Both density states, every year, and both directions lost money.
holdout_policy: 2024-2025 was not evaluated because the unchanged rule failed its development gates.
prohibited_posthoc_changes: using trade counts, clock duration, range, volatility, or another density denominator
adding a density-ratio or displacement threshold
reversing only one transition after observing results
side, weekday, volatility, volume, or regime filters
adding stops or changing execution times
